title: The Center Pawn as a Dangerous Criminal
body: Aron Nimzowitsch, a famous chess master, had a colorful way of teaching strategy. He warned players that an opponent's free center pawn should be treated like a dangerous criminal. In his view, players had to direct all their fury toward this pawn, sentencing it either to death by capturing it or to life imprisonment by blocking it.

variants.lucy: A long time ago, a thoughtful chess master named Aron Nimzowitsch taught his students to look closely at the very middle of the board. He warned that a free pawn marching down the center was like a sneaky troublemaker on the run. To keep your side safe, you had to work together to quietly stop this traveler in its tracks, or gently remove it from the game.
variants.luca: This master, Aron, wanted players to treat that runaway center pawn like an outlaw on the loose! You had to launch a giant mission with your pieces to corner him. Your only choices were to lock him in a deep dungeon so he could never move, or defeat him right on the spot.
variants.cn: 很久以前，爱思考的国际象棋大师阿龙·尼姆佐维奇教学生们，要紧紧盯着棋盘的正中央。他提醒大家：一个沿着中路大步前进、没人拦着的小兵，就像一个正在逃跑的捣蛋鬼。想保住自己的阵地，就得让棋子们齐心协力——要么悄悄把这个“旅行者”拦在半路上，要么干脆请它离开棋盘。

titleCn: 中心兵是个危险的逃犯
